newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul panel mulls unified financial watchdog body.
newsitem.headline: Seoul panel mulls unified financial watchdog body.

text.p: A presidential panel is working on a plan to unify the country's financial supervisory agencies, a statement from the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said on Friday.

The statement said the commission believed a unified agency was needed to cope with possible instability in the financial industry following liberalisation. Currently three separate watchdog bodies supervise the banking, insurance and securities sectors.
One option considered by the commission was an integrated supervisory board that would oversee banks, as well as non-banking financial institutions such as insurance and securities houses.
The other option was to have two supervisory agencies, one watching banks and insurance, and the other securities.
The commission stressed the need for transparency for new entrants into the financial industry. It also said the minimum capital requirements for financial firms should be lowered.
The statement said the presidential panel was considering allowing foreigners to participate in mergers and acquisition of domestic banks.
The commission also said the country's backward credit analysis practices should be modernised.
For example, the commission would propose differentiating corporate interest rates based on independent analysis of companies' credit worthiness.

The commission is due to meet on Saturday to draft the final proposals to be sent to President Kim Young-sam by the end of May. But a commission official said the panel would further refine some proposals next week related to sensitive issues.
All drafts will be finalised on May 23, he said.
